newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-PEREC SAYS SHE WILL NEED MIRACLE TO WIN MEDAL.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-PEREC SAYS SHE WILL NEED MIRACLE TO WIN MEDAL.

text.p: Double Olympic champion Marie-Jose Perec admitted on Wednesday she would need a miracle to win a medal in the women's 200 metres at the world championships after working hard to win her first-round heat.

Perec, who won the 200 and 400 metres titles at last year's Atlanta Olympics, has been in indifferent form all season and had originally decided not to come to the Athens event because she said she had no chance.

Breathing hard after winning in 22.87 seconds, Perec said: "It would need a miracle for me to have a medal. I could have stayed at home but it would have been too hard. Every season I need something to look forward to
"I pushed hard because I had no idea where I stood...That's normal because I haven't entered a competition for four weeks. I feel okay but it is going to be very difficult to get a medal."
There were few surprise in the first-round heats which took place in blistering heat on a sunny morning.
Ukraine's Zhanna Pintussevic, who won the silver medal in the 100 metres at the weekend, easily won her heat in 22.85.
Jamaican veteran Merlene Ottey looked relaxed as she took third in her heat in 22.47 to go through to the second round later in the day.
